Partisan polarization is when political parties and their supporters become more ideologically distant and less willing to compromise.
Yes, in many democracies, especially the U.S., polarization has deepened over the past few decades. Voters are increasingly sorted into parties along ideological and cultural lines.
What are the effects on elections?
Polarization reduces the number of swing voters, makes campaigns more focused on turning out the base, and often results in more negative campaigning.
Absolutely. It can cause legislative gridlock, fewer bipartisan deals, and more distrust between parties, making governing harder even after elections are over.
